data.narrative:
Osaro is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Derik Pridmore and Michael Kahane that has raised $86.8M to date. Valuation assessment draws on a comparison universe of nine private companies and one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) operating in the same sector and stage.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses total capital raised ($87M) as a value proxy and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B progression to the next funding stage, implying a valuation of $165M. Peer-median triangulation examines three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B). The median of this peer set is $1.8B, with a range of $1.6B–$2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide implied range: $140M (stage-progression floor) to $2.0B (peer median high). The median triangulated value across both methods is $957M, reflecting substantial methodological divergence. Key uncertainties include whether Osaro's capital efficiency and market position justify valuation at the peer median level versus early-stage progression multiples, and whether the private peer set accurately reflects comparable risk and growth trajectory. Additional diligence on revenue traction, customer concentration, and technology defensibility would be required to narrow this range.
